tagline: Leading the sustainable transformation of intralogistics
hero_kpi_rationale: The electric segment is the primary growth and sustainability driver for KION, already representing 88.1% of industrial vehicle sales, approaching the strategic target of 90% by 2027.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total annual sales of the company.
kpis.description: Revenue grew 8.2% in 2022, supported by demand for automated and electric logistics solutions.
kpis.signal: Solid growth despite challenging economic environment.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Profit after all charges and taxes.
kpis.description: Net income fell to EUR 105.8 million in 2022 versus EUR 568 million in 2021, impacted by cost increases and exceptional adjustments.
kpis.signal: Sharp decline in net income in 2022.

kpis.name: R&D Spending
kpis.explanation: Total amount of research and development expenditures.
kpis.description: R&D spending reached EUR 321.3 million in 2022, representing 2.9% of revenue, up 17.7% year-over-year.

kpis.name: Total Headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of full-time equivalent (FTE) employees.
kpis.description: Total headcount stood at 41,149 FTE employees at end of 2022, up 3.9% versus 2021.

kpis.name: Electric Vehicle Mix
kpis.explanation: Proportion of industrial vehicles sold by the ITS segment that are electric or fuel cell powered.
kpis.description: 88.1% of industrial vehicles sold by KION in 2022 were electric, up from 87.0% in 2021.
kpis.signal: Leader in electric segment with nearly 90% mix.

kpis.name: GHG Emissions (Scope 1+2)
kpis.explanation: Direct emissions (Scope 1) and energy-related indirect emissions (Scope 2) of the company in CO₂ equivalent.
kpis.description: GHG emissions (Scope 1+2) declined 5.7% in 2022 to 141 kt CO₂e, supported by energy efficiency gains.

kpis.name: GHG Emissions (Scope 3)
kpis.explanation: Indirect emissions related to the value chain, including product use, procurement, and logistics.
kpis.description: Scope 3 emissions decreased 6.5% in 2022 to 18,352 kt CO₂e, reflecting improved product efficiency during use phase.

kpis.name: ISO 14001 Certification Rate
kpis.explanation: Proportion of group sites certified ISO 14001 (environmental management system).
kpis.description: 81% of KION's sites were ISO 14001 certified in 2022, up from 72% in 2021, with target of 100% by 2024.

kpis.name: Electric Vehicle Mix
kpis.explanation: Proportion of industrial vehicles sold by the ITS segment that are electric or fuel cell powered.
kpis.description: Electric mix is progressing steadily, moving from 87.0% in 2021 to 88.1% in 2022.

kpis.name: ISO 14001 Certification Rate
kpis.explanation: Proportion of group sites certified ISO 14001 (environmental management system).
kpis.description: ISO 14001 certification is advancing rapidly, with 81% of sites certified in 2022, targeting 100% by 2024.

risks.title: Product safety and accident prevention
risks.score_rationale: Major risk for KION: 34,051 industrial forklift accidents in Germany in 2021 (51% from collisions), 11 fatalities. Item 1A explicitly details this as a strategic priority. Intensive language: "top priority", "prevent serious or fatal accidents". Trend stable but high categorical weight for logistics sector.

risks.title: Compliance with product safety standards and sectoral standards
risks.score_rationale: Item 1A explicitly mentions "actively drive new safety standards" and compliance with international standards. Strong normative language: "must", "binding". Risk of regulatory non-compliance increasing with evolving EU/national standards. High categorical weight for industrial equipment manufacturer.

risks.title: Supply chain dependency and LkSG compliance
risks.score_rationale: Item 1A explicitly cites "German Supply Chain Duty Act (LkSG)" and supplier audits. Presence in ~40 countries creates complexity. Moderate language but clear legal obligation. Trend up: LkSG strengthened since 2023. Medium-high categorical weight for multinational group.

risks.title: Attraction and retention of qualified talent in automation/digitalization
risks.score_rationale: Item 1A emphasizes "highly qualified and motivated employees are key driver" and training for automation/digitalization changes. Growing headcount (41,149 FTE in 2022 vs 39,602 in 2021). Moderate language but clear strategic importance. Trend up: increased competition for tech talent. Medium categorical weight for industrial sector.

risks.title: Ergonomics and user-centered product design
risks.score_rationale: Item 1A mentions "Ergonomics as a development goal" and "user-oriented, safe and ergonomic products". Moderate language but integrated into product strategy. Trend stable. Medium categorical weight: competitive differentiation but not existential risk.

risks.title: Transition to software solutions and product cybersecurity
risks.score_rationale: Item 1A cites "extend safety product portfolio by software defined solutions". Moderate language but clear digitalization strategy. Trend up: increasing cyber risks for connected products. Medium-high categorical weight for technology transition.

risks.title: Pricing competitiveness of advanced safety functions
risks.score_rationale: Item 1A mentions "attractive pricing for safety features" and "competitive and convincing value proposition". Moderate language. Trend stable. Low-medium categorical weight: pricing positioning issue versus competitors.

risks.title: Reduction of GHG emissions in product portfolio
risks.score_rationale: Item 1A mentions "Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions in products and solutions" as action field. Moderate language but integrated into strategy. Trend up: EU regulation (Fit-for-55) strengthens requirements. Medium categorical weight for industrial manufacturer.

ai_positioning.summary: KION adopts a measured approach to artificial intelligence, progressively integrating AI capabilities into its automated logistics solutions, without making it a central communication focus.
evidence: No explicit mention of AI or machine learning in the 2022 sustainability report
Focus on automation, safety, and electrification rather than AI
Absence of KPIs related to AI adoption or investments
